title: `no-extra-semi` mistakenly removes necessary semicolon when `semi` is `never`

body:
<!--
This template is for bug reports. If you are reporting a bug, please continue on. If you are here for another reason, please see below:

1. To propose a new rule: http://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/new-rules

3. If you have any questions, please stop by our chatroom: https://gitter.im/eslint/eslint

Note that leaving sections blank will make it difficult for us to troubleshoot and we may have to close the issue.
-->

**Tell us about your environment**

* **ESLint Version:**
3.13.1
* **Node Version:**
6.9.3
* **npm Version:**
4.1.1
**What parser (default, Babel-ESLint, etc.) are you using?**
default
**Please show your full configuration:**

<!-- Paste your configuration below: -->
```yaml
rules:
  semi:
    - error
    - never
  no-extra-semi:
    - error
```

**What did you do? Please include the actual source code causing the issue.**

<!-- Paste the source code below: -->
```js
var foo = function(){};
;[1].map(foo)
```

**What did you expect to happen?**
```js
var foo = function(){}
;[1].map(foo)
```
**What actually happened? Please include the actual, raw output from ESLint.**
```js
var foo = function(){}
[1].map(foo)
```

When `semi` is `never`, `no-extra-semi` is true, and there are whitespaces between two semicolons, those rules will delete both of semicolons. `semi` deletes the first one, and `no-extra-semi` deletes the second one.
